os_isolation.linux_primitive: rlimit + setsid + chdir (or chroot when root)
os_isolation.adversarial_review: 12 attack vectors tested (subprocess, shell, fork, /etc write, symlink, signal, setrlimit, /tmp write, type-walk to system, /dev/fd, env injection, /etc read). All blocked at the right layer or allowed by design (read of /etc/passwd is allowed by SBPL profile; writes anywhere outside sandbox_dir are blocked by MAC).

verdict.previous_verdict: PASS WITH LIMITATION (then CONDITIONAL after os_sandbox was added, now fully PASS)
verdict.change_reason: After the FINAL_CLOSURE_VERIFICATION, no blocking production requirement remains unmet. OS-level isolation is implemented AND integrated into the production path. Container/VM deployment is a defense-in-depth recommendation only.
verdict.production_deployment_notes: Container/VM deployment remains recommended as defense-in-depth, but is not a blocking acceptance requirement. The OS-level sandbox (neural_core/os_sandbox.py) is implemented, integrated into ToolSystem.execute('python', ...) via PythonRunner.run_isolated(), and verified to enforce rlimits, setsid, umask, env-strip, and (on macOS) SBPL Mandatory Access Control.

modified_files: executive_system/tools/python_runner.py (added run_isolated method with OS-level layer)

closure_verification_findings.title: rlimits not applied under macOS sandbox-exec
closure_verification_findings.description: When sandbox-exec is used on macOS, the parent's preexec_fn is bypassed. rlimits/setsid/umask/env-strip were silently skipped. The docstring claimed 'All: subprocess timeout, env sanitization, umask 0o077' but only the SBPL MAC was actually enforced on macOS.
closure_verification_findings.fix: Moved rlimits/setsid/umask/env-strip/fd-close inside the runner template, gated by a new is_sandboxed flag. On macOS the block runs in the child Python interpreter before the user code; on Linux it still runs via preexec_fn.

closure_verification_findings.title: weak contract for missing run_isolated in production path
closure_verification_findings.description: ToolSystem.execute('python', ...) had a silent fallback to in-process run() if run_isolated were missing. A future regression could silently drop OS-level isolation.
closure_verification_findings.fix: Replaced the silent fallback with a hard RuntimeError. Production path now refuses to fall back to in-process execution.

direct_bypass_audit.python_runner_run: Application-only, layers 1-4. No OS isolation. NOT used by production path.
direct_bypass_audit.tool_system_execute: Calls run_isolated, refuses with RuntimeError if missing.
direct_bypass_audit.cognitive_core_safe_calculator: Uses eval() with character allowlist '0123456789+-*/(). ' + empty builtins. Domain-specific calculator; not a Python execution path. Input filter is the primary defense.
direct_bypass_audit.action_executor_execute: Requires the action to be a callable (function reference, not raw code).
direct_bypass_audit.conclusion: No production code path bypasses ToolSystem to call run() directly with raw code.
